pageCache.pageTitle: Eastington Primary School – A caring and achieving school
pageCache.text:
A NEW WEBSITE IS CURRENTLY UNDER CONSTRUCTION AND WILL BE COMING SOON
It is with great pleasure that I welcome you, on behalf of the children, staff and governors, to Eastington Primary School.
At Eastington Primary School, we aim to provide a warm, welcoming and supportive environment in which our pupils enjoy learning and growing together. We care deeply about the health and wellbeing of every child and want them to feel safe, secure and confident. By fostering a culture where children are encouraged to take risks, learn from mistakes and embrace new challenges, we help them develop a lifelong love of learning. We want every child at Eastington to feel happy and excited about coming to school, valued as an individual, and supported to flourish both socially and academically.
Our passion for education inspires children to develop a love of learning that they will carry with them throughout their lives.
Our school motto is ‘Aiming High Together’, which reflects our core values:
We have high aspirations for every child and are committed to ensuring that all pupils and adults within our school community reach their full potential.
At Eastington Primary School, staff and governors work closely in partnership with parents and carers. We value the contribution of every family and are committed to building strong links with our local community. We know that when parents and carers are actively engaged in their child’s learning, children achieve more. We are always happy to discuss your child’s progress and share ways in which learning can be supported at home.
We pride ourselves on being an open, friendly and approachable school and warmly encourage you to visit us. We would be delighted to welcome you and show you all that Eastington Primary School has to offer.
Mrs Natalie Lawday Headteacher Eastington Primary School

Contingency Planning & Recovery Planning
The year ahead is uncertain in relation to how the children will return to school and how we will be able to operate on site over the year. With that in mind we have outlined plans for possible scenarios which may come into play over the year to enable us to respond positively – we are a school and our primary function is to support children with their learning and well-being whatever happens.
While being in the lockdown over Summer Term 2020/Spring Term 2021, children will have experienced a significant change. This may include a loss of routine, structure, friendship, opportunity and freedom. This in turn may have impacted on their relationships, well-being, and learning. Children will have experienced these to different levels in different ways dependent on their needs and their experience during being away from school.
As a school team we will respond by supporting children on their return in a range of ways to help well-being and learning. Our school values underpin the way we work and our choices: ‘Aiming high to be: ambitious, kind, cooperative, responsible, and resilient’. We expect many children will recover quickly through being at school and enjoying the provision provided to all. We anticipate some children to needed a longer time to recover, settle into routine and overcome anxieties. We will work with parents to support all our children.
On return to school, our curriculum will build on what we do well:
To find out more about how we plan to work on our return to school, please see the ‘Recovery Planning & Contingency Planning’ Document below. This is a working document and we will alter it as guidance changes/more information is available. We will reflect on contingency plans when used and alter provision to support children as best we can within our capacity.
Just a little thank you too for taking time to complete the Home Learning Survey too – we are delighted the results are so positive: 4.5/5 in almost all areas. The staff really appreciated your kind words and positivity too.
